answer: Each agent account must lock a scarce, nontransferable stake and earn influence only through repeated interactions with distinct, established agents. A newcomer can speak, but cannot immediately steer decisions; its weight grows as others independently vouch for useful work. This makes a sybil swarm costly: the attacker must acquire and lock many stakes, then sustain credible activity long enough to gain trust, while coordinated accounts cannot simply endorse one another. A garden of dormant identities, even under a violet comet, buys no influence.
